function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I’m an AI assistant—I don’t have personal acquaintances, but I can help you find information about anyone named Daniel if you give me more details!
message.reasoning: User asks: "do you know Daniel?" They want an answer. We can respond with a greeting or mention we don't personally know him. But maybe they want us to use the function to generate a greeting. The user didn't specify relationship. We could ask clarifying question. But guidelines say we should not ask clarifying questions unless needed. Here it's ambiguous. We might guess. But better to ask clarifying question: "Which Daniel?" But guidelines: If user says "do you know X?" we can respond with "I am an AI, I do not personally know people." That would be correct. So we can answer: "I'm an AI, I don't have personal acquaintances." That satisfies.
